bet.text: A floor coral intake, and a claw that can score from both sides, so the robot cycles fast without driving far or turning around.

demand.text: The end-of-week-1 list marked processor, coral L1 to L4, floor and station intake and scoring on both sides as needed, and the net as not to pursue; scoring in the net was added later. The team weighed points, ease of design and ranking points.
For worlds qualification matches it put ranking points in this order: auto, barge, wins, coral.

auto.text: Four routines: L4 coral from the human player; a drive-by version that drops the preload in L1 on the way past; a floor intake auto for three pieces that leaves the station to partners; and a centre auto for one L4 coral and two algae in the net.

cycle.text: The floor intake turns coral to one orientation and tosses it up into the claw. Elevator, shoulder and wrist take it to a level on either side while the robot aligns from AprilTags. The wrist flips for L1 so it can shoot over coral already there.

endgame.text: The robot drives into the cage until sprung hooks latch. The climber then rotates the cage until the chain is above the robot's centre of gravity.
The worlds plan was a deep climb in every match. Its playoff section allows a fast scorer to skip the climb in a very unlikely case.

fallback.text: If the floor intake breaks, the wrist lets the claw load at the human player station. The operator can also flip the wrist when coral sits wrong.

gave_up.text: Handing coral from one mechanism to another added significant complexity, and the robot was not designed for defense.
The biggest challenge was packaging a wide intake beside a centred elevator, with the climber, inside the frame perimeter.

changed.text: After two events a U-shaped plate replaced the elevator's top crossbar, the intake ramps were redrawn in CAD to stop jams, and the claw got longer plates, algae shields and harder wheels. A separate algae floor intake was dropped.
The goals review says lack of auto consistency created severe deficits by worlds.
Coral intake, algae intake and elevator all needed major revisions after the beta robot.

outcome.text: 54-12-0 in official play; ranked 15 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 102.88, Archimedes).

facts.text: Each module drives with a Kraken X60 and turns with a Falcon 500
Maximum speed with the X3 ratio
Square frame side

functions.name: Belly pan and wiring

solves.text: Keep wires accessible when there is little space in the drivebase

functions.type: aluminium belly pan with power wires underneath

facts.text: Belly pan thickness, with a lightening pattern for electrical routing and weight
Printed WAGO mounts on the modules keep CAN wires short, so a failure at one module does not take out the whole loop

functions.name: Coral floor intake

solves.text: Pick up coral from the floor in any orientation and centre it before it enters the frame

functions.type: sprung over-the-bumper roller with ramps and vertical rollers

facts.text: Front roller uses compliant wheels of this diameter
Surgical tubing on the sides gives even pressure for any coral orientation
Passive ramps and vertical rollers centre the coral
One Kraken X60 through a 2.5:1 belt drives the rollers; a Falcon 500 deploys it
The outer two passive vertical rollers have silicone tubing and the center one does not, so coral spins in place until it is centered, drops off the ramp onto the silicone and climbs
Roller size and spacing leave a coral that arrives end-on only one point of contact, so it pivots sideways; it sometimes sticks for a moment first
The wave plate added to the comp robot does no centering: it blocks the position where coral got stuck between the rollers
The ramps are bent to approximate an ideal centering curve, which also helps coral center as it climbs
A belted reduction between the sets of intake wheels keeps their surface speeds about equal

cost.text: Coral occasionally jammed at the first two events, needing the driver or operator and sometimes slowing cycles; roller and ramp changes followed
The intake mounts shifted, so the motor mount had to be adjustable; the team does not recommend it and says a motor should share a plate with its critical gears

functions.name: Handoff

solves.text: Join a wide floor intake to an end effector that also loads at the station

functions.type: floor intake tosses coral into a waiting claw

facts.text: The intake rotates coral to a consistent orientation on the ground, then tosses it up into the claw

functions.name: Claw

solves.text: Take coral and algae with one mechanism that owns a piece as soon as it touches it

functions.type: roller claw for coral and algae

facts.text: Compliant wheel diameter
Coral compression
One Kraken X60 through 8.125:1, changed from 9.3:1 between events
Weight without the wrist
Weight with the wrist
A beam break detects pieces; a limit switch was inconsistent on algae
The X60 was used because the X44s the team bought did not arrive in time, and the ratio was designed around the X60

cost.text: Softer 35A wheels wore and algae rolled out, until 50A wheels and algae shields were fitted

functions.name: Elevator

solves.text: Reach the floor, the station and every reef level from a limited stow height

functions.type: continuous elevator strung with Dyneema rope

facts.text: Vertical extension
Two Kraken X60s at 3:1 on a 1.5 in spool
Two drive strings and one return string; springs and a ratcheting wrench set tension
Pulleys are printed in CF-nylon with two bearings each
Each rope is tied around a bolt and washer, which tighten into a rivnut in the spool tube to clamp it
Aluminum arms set the angle at which rope meets the spool, and a second set of redirects near the top lines it up with the pulleys

cost.text: Plates and the top tube warped outward at the first two events, letting the stage and carriage move sideways; a U-shaped cross-plate replaced the tube
Before the redirect arms the rope sometimes doubled up or ran off the end of the spool; clearances there stayed tight, and the team would move the spool farther from the elevator

functions.name: Shoulder

solves.text: Move the claw between opposite sides of the robot with little backlash

functions.type: arm pivot on a custom lantern gear

facts.text: One Kraken X60 through 45:1
An absolute encoder on a follower gear tracks the arm
The lantern gear was made on the team's CNC router
About 20 thousandths were taken off the lantern gear tooth tips so it passes smoothly from tooth to tooth, a precaution that had worked on the off-season robot

solves.text: Turn coral from its loading orientation to its scoring orientation and keep it clear of the elevator when changing sides

facts.text: Rotation each way
One Falcon 500 through 21.4:1
Solid aluminium dead-axle shaft

functions.name: Climber

solves.text: Hold the cage securely and lift the robot without changing its orientation

functions.type: levering deep-cage climber with sprung harpoon hooks

facts.text: The team lists a 3 second climb plus cage acquisition
Weight
One Kraken X60; the binder gives 687.5:1 on one page and 675:1 on another
Folds flat in the drive base
The printed CF-nylon tensioner held up, and the team is fairly certain it was never replaced

cost.text: Smaller acquisition area, listed as the con of levering; a polycarbonate wing was added to funnel the cage
Gears skipped and wore at the first event, so the final stage became chain

solves.text: Move several joints through shared space without damage

facts.text: Computes future collisions of wrist, arm, intake and elevator and blocks those moves
The wrist turns late on the way to L1 so it does not hit the elevator
Tested in simulation with AdvantageScope

cost.text: Many state transitions brought edge cases, so the operator got a wrist flip control

solves.text: Align to the reef precisely and correct errors in auto

facts.text: Limelight cameras
Odometry runs on its own thread at 5 times the speed of the main code
When aligning to the reef it uses single-tag estimates from the camera facing it

decisions.choice: Two acquisition mechanisms, a floor intake and a claw that loads at the station
decisions.because: prototypes showed a wide over-the-bumper intake was best on the floor but wrong for the station

decisions.choice: Sprung over-the-bumper intake with ramps and vertical rollers
decisions.because: it takes coral in any orientation, centres it and avoids clogging with several coral
decisions.cost: coral still jammed occasionally at the first two events; a wave plate similar to the rejected one was added after the first

decisions.choice: Roller claw with two driven rollers
decisions.because: it takes and holds algae as well as coral
decisions.instead_of: a pinch claw and a single roller
decisions.cost: algae rolled out until shields and harder wheels were fitted after the second event

decisions.because: the team had a history of good arms but not of strong elevators
decisions.cost: an added wrist to turn the piece

decisions.choice: Constantly sprung harpoon hooks, without the earlier deploying latch, on a levering climber
decisions.because: it was simpler, had fewer parts prone to breaking and performed similarly
a broken elevator would also have cost the climb
decisions.instead_of: a dual-purpose climber on the scoring mechanism

decisions.because: it cannot slip or skip, has very low backlash and can be made in house on the CNC router
it was not significantly better than the claw and added motors and sensors

decisions.choice: Build three robots: Alpha, Beta and Comp
decisions.because: programmers could start in week 1, mechanisms were iterated on a robot instead of alone, and problems showed early enough to revise
decisions.cost: a fast, stressful schedule; the comp robot finished about 8 days late, mostly on purpose, to spend more time with the beta

decisions.choice: Fill the reef pegs closest to the robot
decisions.because: the worlds plan holds that a floor-loading robot scores more points per second that way
the team wanted to minimize backlash and weight on the arm
decisions.cost: a VersaPlanetary stayed in; it helps with neither, and the team would probably try to remove it

decisions.choice: Zero the wrist against a hard stop by current draw
decisions.because: the team wanted to explore it, though some were nervous, and it ended up working great
decisions.instead_of: a beam break, designed in case it was needed and then left off
